mainEntity.name: Is it normal for a new dental implant crown to feel high at first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some initial awareness or sensitivity around a newly placed implant crown is common. The mouth is highly attuned to changes, and it can take a short period for the brain to adjust to the new restoration. However, if the implant consistently feels elevated when biting — particularly if this is accompanied by discomfort — it is worth having the bite assessed by your dentist. Minor adjustments to the crown's occlusal surface are routine and straightforward to perform.

mainEntity.name: How does a dentist check if a dental implant bite is too high?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dentists typically use a material called articulating paper to assess bite height. This thin paper is placed between the teeth, and the patient is asked to bite down. The pressure marks left on the crown and surrounding teeth reveal which surfaces are making contact and whether any single point is taking disproportionate force. Based on this information, the dentist can make precise, targeted adjustments to the crown surface to achieve a balanced bite.

mainEntity.name: Can a high implant bite cause damage over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: If a significant bite discrepancy remains unaddressed over an extended period, it can place mechanical stress on the implant components and surrounding bone. It may also contribute to discomfort in the jaw joint or muscles. However, most bite discrepancies are identified and resolved at routine follow-up appointments without causing lasting issues. Seeking an early assessment if you are concerned is always the most straightforward approach.

mainEntity.name: Will bite adjustment affect the appearance of my implant crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, a minor occlusal adjustment involves removing a very small amount of material from the biting surface of the crown — an area that is generally not visible during normal smiling or speaking. The aesthetic appearance of the crown is typically unaffected by bite adjustments. Your dentist will discuss what the adjustment involves before proceeding.

mainEntity.name: How long after implant placement should I wait before reporting a high bite?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you feel that the bite is clearly uncomfortable or noticeably uneven immediately after placement, there is no need to wait — you can contact your dental practice at any point. It is reasonable to allow a few days for initial post-treatment sensitivity to settle before making a definitive judgement on bite comfort. However, if the sensation is not improving after one to two weeks, arranging a review appointment is advisable. There is no benefit to delaying assessment if the discomfort is persistent.

mainEntity.name: Can dental implant bite problems be related to peri-implantitis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Peri-implantitis is an inflammatory condition affecting the gum and bone tissue surrounding a dental implant, typically associated with bacterial infection rather than bite height. However, because excessive occlusal force may contribute to stress on the bone-implant interface, there can be indirect associations between unresolved bite issues and implant health over time. If you are experiencing symptoms such as swelling, bleeding around the implant site, or looseness of the crown, these warrant prompt professional assessment as they may suggest a different underlying concern. If you would like to understand more about implant health and gum care, speaking with a dental professional is the most reliable approach.
